import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
import io

# Load the dataset from the string
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a professional and clean theme for the visualization
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationships between variables
# - x-axis: Hour of the day to show temporal patterns
# - y-axis: Transaction amount
# - hue: Differentiate by transaction type
# - style: Differentiate by fraud status (though all are non-fraudulent in this sample)
# - size: Emphasize the magnitude of the transaction amount
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='hour_of_day',
    y='amount',
    hue='transaction_type',
    style='is_fraud',
    size='amount',
    sizes=(100, 1000),  # Define a range for marker sizes
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and impact ---

# Set an informative title and clear axis labels
ax.set_title('Analysis of Transactions by Time, Type, and Amount', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=13)
ax.set_ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=13)

# Format the y-axis to represent currency
formatter = mtick.FormatStrFormatter('$%1.2f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Set x-axis limits to represent a full 24-hour day and improve readability
ax.set_xlim(-1, 24)
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 25, 2))

# Improve the legend by moving it outside the plot area to avoid overlap
ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to make room for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the resulting visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close(fig)
